newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks in second straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks in second straight record close.

text.p: The Mexican bourse posted its second record close in a row on Tuesday as a steady stream of emerging market funds sought a haven in Mexico after being flushed out of Asia by devaluation woes there.
"The outlook is still very positive. We are still seeing flows towards Latin America, which have mainly bailed out of Asia," said Carlos Fritsch, an equity strategist at the Interacciones brokerage.
The blue-chip IPC share index ended up 47.78 points, or 0.93 percent, to a record 5,183.02. The bourse has now set 46 closing records this year.
"Mexican equities are still attractively valued, and have interesting potential returns," Fritsch added.
Dealers said trading volume of 138.6 million shares was less than seen during last week's flood of buying, but showed demand was still strong.
On the broad market, gainers outpaced decliners by 75 to 37, out of 126 stocks that changed hands.
Analysts said the bourse shrugged off forecast gains in domestic primary rates later in the day as a temporary spike.
Nine money market traders surveyed by Reuters predicted banco de Mexico would raise bellwether 28-day Cetes rates by an average of 75 basis points to 18.45 percent.

The bourse barely reacted to the day's rise in U.S. long bond yields, analysts added, as they were still relatively low and not taken to herald a rise in U.S. base rates at the Federal Reserve's Aug. 19 policy-setting meeting.
Financial group Bancomer accounted for the lion's share of dealing after news the firm had reached a deal to sell tourist venues worth $133 million, dealers said.

Bancomer B shares gained 14 centavos (2 cents) to 5.74 pesos (74 cents), while the cheaper A series climbed 48 centavos (6 cents) to 3.90 pesos (50 cents). The two series accounted for more than 30 percent of all shares traded.
Dealers noted construction and cement firms gained strongly, boosted by speculation the government was planning to restructure debts for companies holding highway concessions.
Construction firm Empresas ICA Sociedad Controladora gained 45 centavos (6 cents) to 25.20 pesos ($3.23), and cement maker Cemex climbed 70 centavos (9 cents) to 42.25 pesos ($5.41).
Dealers said gains by Bancomer and the construction companies outweighed profit-taking on market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico, which shed 10 centavos to end at 21.65 pesos.
